bottom_line: The grid column holds 48 of the 57 sites we could place. Almost every Indonesian data centre runs on PLN, PLN Batam or an estate utility, with diesel only as standby. 22 of the 48 don't say where their power comes from and report no generation of their own.

Estate utilities matter more than expected. Cikarang Listrindo, a private utility inside five Bekasi estates, supplies DCI's main campus: Rp396.8 bn of DCI's Rp457.8 bn electricity cost in 2025. It also supplies PDG's Cibitung campus, and a 2021 report lists NTT and the site EdgeConneX later bought among its customers. In Batam, Nongsa Digital Park runs its own estate grid.

Own power is rare and small. One 1.45 MW site, SpaceDC JAK2, was built to run on its own gas engine. DCI's Karawang campus has a solar farm of up to 30 MW. The Batam solar deals and DCI's 1 GW self-powered park on Bintan are still plans.

Builders' own filings name who builds most big campuses. Total Bangun Persada builds for STT GDC, and in joint jobs whose code names match Microsoft's JKT11 halls (with Shimizu) and Digital Edge's first CGK building (with Accesstech). Acset holds SMX01's Rp802.9 bn building contract and built BDx's CGK3A and CGK4 shells; PT PP built Telkom's Cikarang site and, with Adhi Karya, Nxera Batam. Still unnamed: the builders of PDG's JC3 and JC4, DayOne's Kabil park, BDx CGK5 and the AWS halls, and any genset or UPS maker at a 2025–26 campus.
The rules explain the shape. A data centre may buy power only from its area's utility, wheeling isn't allowed yet, and the capped gas price goes to estate utilities, not to a data centre's own plant.

rules.title: Only the area's utility may sell you power
rules.text: Each business area has one licensed seller, PLN almost everywhere. A data centre can't sign a power deal with an independent producer, even its own subsidiary.
rules.quote: data centers could not enter corporate PPAs directly with independent power producers (IPPs), even if the IPPs are their own subsidiaries.

rules.title: An own plant over 500 kW needs a licence
rules.text: Captive generation above 500 kW needs an own-use licence (IUPTLS). ESDM says the captive plans it licenses are mostly coal.
rules.quote: wajib dimiliki oleh Pelaku Usaha yang menjalankan kegiatan Usaha Penyediaan Tenaga Listrik untuk kepentingan sendiri dengan total kapasitas pembangkit tenaga listrik lebih dari 500 (lima ratus) kilowatt dalam 1 (satu) sistem instalasi tenaga listrik

rules.title: No wheeling yet
rules.text: Moving your own clean power over PLN's lines isn't regulated. Parliament extended the renewables bill (RUU EBET) again in September 2026 instead of passing it.
rules.quote: DPR RI menyetujui perpanjangan waktu pembahasan Rancangan Undang-Undang (RUU) tentang Energi Baru dan Energi Terbarukan (EBET)

rules.title: Rooftop solar runs on PLN's quota
rules.text: Under Permen ESDM 2/2024 the utility sets five-year quotas and approves each system, and exported power isn't credited against the bill.
rules.quote: will not be taken into account in determining the electricity bill of the customer.

rules.title: Cheap gas skips data centres
rules.text: The capped gas price of US$6/MMBtu goes to seven industries and public-supply utilities. Estate utilities such as Cikarang Listrindo and Bekasi Power get it; a data centre's own gas plant doesn't.
rules.quote: Kementerian ESDM Tetapkan 12 Perusahaan Listrik Penerima Gas Murah HGBT

rules.title: Estate utilities hold their own areas
rules.text: Cikarang Listrindo has a public-supply licence for five Bekasi estates, which is why it, not PLN, supplies the data centres there. Batam is its own area too, run by PLN Batam.
rules.quote: an “Integrated Business Permit to Supply Electricity to Public (IUPTLU)” to supply power to the 5 (five) industrial estates in the Bekasi Regency.

method: Six research agents searched on 16 Oct 2026 (UTC), starting from the 44 projects in our 15 Oct report on data centres and the grid. With the sites they added, the map holds 72.

A second pass the same day read builders' and owners' own filings: Telkom's 20-F, the annual reports and financial statements of Total Bangun Persada, Acset, PT PP, DSSA and DCI, plus contractor project pages and vendor case studies. It took the map from 67 to 114 vendor links, most of them builders.

A third check on 17 Oct 2026 (UTC) came before the builders' third-quarter statements, which are due by 31 Oct. It swapped in Adhi Karya's own June statement as the source for its share of Nxera Batam. We found no supplier named in DayOne's US listing prospectus, and PLN Batam hasn't said who won the job to lay a 150 kV cable to a DayOne substation.

Each vendor line links to the page that says so. Confirmed: the vendor, the operator or an official document says it. Reported: news or trade press. Site inferred: the source names the vendor and the job but not the site exactly; the line says how we matched it. Snippet: seen in search results; the page itself couldn't be opened.

Estate utilities count as grid supply, because their plants sit outside the data centre's fence. A bought, already-running data centre counts as brownfield. A site that doesn't disclose its power and reports no generation of its own sits in the grid column with a dashed outline.
Tenants (Oracle, Firmus, Gorilla Technology) are shown, but their megawatts aren't added to cell totals. MW figures are IT or facility load, as each source gives them.
Left out: PDN Batam (cancelled Feb 2025), in-house server rooms such as Hutama Karya's, and power-plant contracts that don't serve a named data centre.
Not found isn't the same as absent: most operators don't publish their suppliers, and several news sites (Bisnis, Kontan, DCD) blocked our reader.
The cell pictures are AI illustrations made for this page, not photos of the projects.

webs.title: DCI Indonesia
webs.bottom_line:
DCI is still controlled by its three founders (Toto Sugiri 29.9%, Marina Budiman 22.5%, Han Arming Hanafia 14.1%), with Anthoni Salim at 11.1% since May 2021, but its growth outside Cibitung runs on Salim money: Salim's DISM and DISP own the H2 Karawang and E1 Jakarta buildings, which DCI operates for a 10-15% revenue share and rents capacity in (Rp264.8 bn in 2025, 22.7% of its cost of revenues), and Salim's Gallant Venture is co-developing the 1,000 MW Bintan park.
Power at the main Cibitung campus comes from the estate utility Cikarang Listrindo (Rp396.8 bn, 87% of DCI's 2025 electricity bill), plus DCI's own licensed standby generation; no DCI filing names PLN.
PT Sumaraja Indah built JK3, JK5 and JK6. The money now comes from BCA, which replaced Bank Mandiri in 2026 with up to Rp18.6 tn of investment loans to build capacity that customers have already contracted.

webs.title: BDx Indonesia
webs.bottom_line:
BDx Indonesia (PT Starone Mitra Telekomunikasi) has been 75% owned since 2 June 2022 by I Squared Capital's BDx (through BDX Asia Data Center Holdings, Singapore), with Indosat at 17.5% and its subsidiary Lintasarta at 7.5%, and Bloomberg reported in February 2026 that I Squared was weighing a sale of BDx at about US$2 billion.
All of its power is PLN grid supply under a 2 June 2026 contract for about 1.2 GW (CGK4 788, now 845 MVA, through a new 150 kV substation PLN is building at Jatiluhur; CGK3A about 60 MVA; CGK5 385 MVA), while the "renewable-powered" Jatiluhur label rests only on unsigned hydropower talks with Perum Jasa Tirta II, and West Java stopped the 640 MW CGK4 expansion over missing AMDAL and PBG permits and its draw on Jatiluhur reservoir water.
Acset (Astra group) built the CGK3A and CGK4 shells and Bank Permata, BCA and KB Bank lead its debt (US$320 million, April 2026), but no public source names a tenant other than its own shareholders, an equipment maker or a commissioner.

webs.title: NeutraDC
webs.bottom_line: NeutraDC (PT Telkom Data Ekosistem) has been 100% Telkom since Telkom bought Telkomsigma's last 19.19% in September 2026, and Telkom (52% held through Danantara) is now weighing binding offers to sell a stake by end-2026, while its Batam growth site is already a joint venture with Singtel's Nxera (35.63%) and Medco Power (about 3%). All firm power comes from PLN: its GIIC 150 kV data-centre substation feeds Cikarang (plus an August 2026 MoU for up to 200 MW more) and a 90 MVA premium PLN Batam contract feeds Batam, while the green supply is still certificates and MoUs (PLN RECs, Pertamina, Medco solar). State contractors built the shells (PT PP at Cikarang for Rp314 bn, a PP-Adhi joint operation at Batam for Rp746 bn), and ZTE and Huawei hold the "Delta Project" fit-out contracts that most likely sit in Cikarang.

webs.title: Digital Edge
webs.bottom_line: Digital Edge Indonesia (PT Ekagrata Data Gemilang) is 99.83% owned by Indonet, 92.10% of which belongs to Digital Edge's two Hong Kong companies, now taking it private at Rp11,500 a share; Indonet's 2025 annual report traces control up to Stonepeak entities that co-founder Michael Dorrell controls 100%. The 500 MW CGK campus sits in separate Indonet project companies, which bought Rp741.5 bn of GIIC land from Puradelta Lestari (Sinar Mas Land and Sojitz) and borrowed US$665 m from eight banks led by BCA, Credit Agricole and DBS, plus US$530.2 m from eleven lenders in September 2026. Its power comes only from PLN (2 x 725 MVA on redundant feeds, through the new 350 MVA GI Sukamahi substation); no CGK tenant is named anywhere, CoreWeave included, and the only named builder is a Total Bangun Persada and Accesstech joint operation on a "GAIA" project, which we match to CGK.

webs.title: DayOne
webs.bottom_line: DayOne is no longer a GDS company: its 5 Oct 2026 F-1 lists Coatue and Hillhouse at 19.5% each, GDS at 19.4% after selling US$385 mn of shares back in Jan 2026, and Achi Capital at 15.6%. Its Batam business sits in PT DayOne Data Centers Indonesia, owned 60% by DayOne and 40% by Indonesia's sovereign fund INA, which also put money into DayOne itself in the Series C (most likely US$200 mn through PT Lestari Investasi Indonesia). Both campuses are on Citramas estates: the 72 MW Nongsa campus (let to "a leading U.S. hyperscaler", reportedly Oracle; structure built by Astra's Acset; financed by a Rp6.7 tn DBS/UOB loan) takes power through Tamarin's estate grid, while Kabil has its own 511 MVA PLN Batam contract for 360 MW of IT capacity, 240 MW of it already contracted and most likely for Firmus's NVIDIA AI factory.

webs.title: Princeton Digital Group
webs.bottom_line: PDG's five old enterprise sites came from XL Axiata in 2019 through a joint venture, PT Princeton Digital Group Data Centres, in which XL kept 14.82% after 2022; on 12 Oct 2026 PDG agreed to sell those sites to Sinar Mas's SM+. Its hyperscale arm, PT Princeton Digital Group, owns JC2 and paid Sinarmas Land's Puradelta Lestari about Rp618 bn for the JC3 and JC4 land in GIIC, so Sinar Mas both sold PDG its new land and is buying its old sites. Power comes from estate grids and PLN, not PDG's own plants (Cikarang Listrindo at Cibitung with up to 20% biomass from a coal co-firing plant, a PLN bay of up to 200 MVA at GI Sukamahi for JC3, Tamarin and PLN Batam for the unbuilt Batam campus), and no builder or equipment maker is named for any Indonesian site.

webs.title: STT GDC
webs.bottom_line: STT GDC Indonesia (PT STT GDC Indonesia) is a joint venture with Triputra and Temasek, and STT GDC controls it. Since 31 Aug 2026, STT GDC itself is owned 75% by KKR and 25% by Singtel, after a S$6.6 bn buyout of ST Telemedia, but Temasek has not left: it is still a direct JV partner and owns about 51.69% of Singtel. The 374 MW campus in GIIC is powered only by PLN, through PLN's shared 120 MVA "Data Center" substation (Amazon, Microsoft, Komdigi and Telkom use it too) and STT's own on-campus 150 kV substation; no contracted MVA has been published, and the renewable plan with PLN has no stated form or size. Total Bangun Persada builds it on its "Iris" contracts, and STT was that contractor's biggest customer in 2025 (Rp801.7 bn, 20.55% of revenue); the land was bought from Sinar Mas's Puradelta (Rp210.8 bn in 2025), and the build is funded by an IDR 8.8 tn loan from OCBC, HSBC and BNI with a green tranche.

webs.title: SM+ (Sinar Mas)
webs.bottom_line: Franky Oesman Widjaja controls DSSA (59.9% through PT Sinar Mas Tunggal), which owns SM+ outright, but SM+'s flagship SMX01 is a joint venture in which Korea's KIRA holds about half; LG Sinar Mas (the LG CNS joint venture) designs it, installs its Rp1.23 tn of electrical, cooling and IT systems and will run it, Acset puts up the Rp803 bn building, and the money comes from about Rp1.1 tn of DSSA bonds and sukuk plus a Rp2.97 tn Mandiri loan. No Sinar Mas power plant feeds it: DSSA sold its captive plants to the APP paper mills in 2024 and 75% of its three coal IPPs (which sell to PLN outside Java) to China's Datang in 2020, so SMX01's power deal is with PLN's Jakarta unit. The edge network is about 10 MW of former Smartfren buildings, not the 43 MW analysts cite, and Sinar Mas's bigger data-centre role is as landlord: its Kota Deltamas estate sold GIIC land to Microsoft, AWS, PDG, STT GDC and others, and data-centre buyers made up 94% of the estate company's land sales in H1 2026.
